summary: UCSB describes new console attachments for its IBM 360/75 through an interface called the MLC/360M, which gives 32 independently addressed I/O connections in 16 pairs for devices over RS-232 style signals. It explains the first group of attachments.

plainLanguage.summary: The MLC/360M connects many kinds of devices to UCSB's IBM 360/75. Its separate input and output paths let the computer work with several terminal types and modems.

which terminals did ucsb connect to its host
subtitle: An interface for connecting many device types to the UCSB host

tldr.problem: UCSB wanted its IBM 360/75 to connect to a range of terminals and other input/output devices.
tldr.mechanism: The MLC/360M provides independently addressed input and output connections on the computer's Multiplexor Channel, using EIA signal levels.
tldr.outcome: The notice describes the interface and reports its use with different modems and display terminals.

today: RFC 311 describes the MLC/360M interface and console attachments at UCSB. It reports the devices the lab had connected or was evaluating at the time.

sections.title: The MLC/360M Interface
sections.content: The Multi-Line Controller/360M is an interface unit attached to the Multiplexor Channel of UCSB's 360. It provides 32 independently addressed I/O connections arranged in 16 pairs for full-duplex use. Each input group has a 16-bit buffer, and each output group has a 32-bit buffer.
sections.plainLanguage: The interface gives the computer many separate paths for sending and receiving data. The paired paths can carry input and output at the same time.

sections.title: Adaptable Device Connections
sections.content:
Devices connect through a data-set type connector, and the I/O signal levels follow the EIA RS-232 specification. The notice says both the hardware groups and their supporting software can be changed to accommodate non-standard devices.

The first implementation supported 201B data-sets at 2400 baud in a time-shared environment.
sections.plainLanguage: The interface uses RS-232 signal levels and can be adjusted for devices that do not fit its original setup. It first supported 201B data-sets.

sections.title: Terminals and Other Uses
sections.content: UCSB had modified I/O groups for a range of uses, from 300-baud acoustic-coupled connections to 9600-baud classroom operation. The notice also describes a Tektronix 4002A terminal that could use upper- and lower-case ASCII and a General Purpose Graphics Terminal that UCSB was evaluating in its online system.
sections.plainLanguage: UCSB adapted the interface for both slow and faster connections. It also used it with text and graphics terminals.
